gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the FOSSiBOT F2400's 2,048 Wh is cell energy, not AC energy: FOSSiBOT's own FAQ sizes runtime at Watt-Hours × 0.85 (1,741 Wh), and techtest.org (Michael Barton) measured only 1,512 Wh (74%) from the AC outlet at a 100 W load.
standout_why: Compared against cheapestwh.com (cited, read through the r.jina.ai proxy) and the Slickdeals ECO-WORTHY PS2400 thread (opened directly). cheapestwh has part of it: a generic rule that a 1,000 Wh station runs a 100 W fridge about 8.5 hours 'after inverter losses', and 'multiply by 1.3 for inverter losses and a reserve'. It ranks the F2400 on rated Wh ($0.292/Wh) and gives no maker formula and no measured figure for any model. The Slickdeals thread gives no usable-capacity, efficiency or idle figure. The three cited outletpicks.com URLs, powerstationgearlab.com and our own dealectric.com page could not be opened (certificate error, then a Cloudflare 403 through the proxy), so the score is judged against cheapestwh and Slickdeals only and could drop to 1 if outletpicks carries usable-Wh figures.
decides: It confirms the F2400 as the under-$600 pick but changes what the shopper is buying. By FOSSiBOT's own formula they get about 1,741 Wh of AC energy, which is $0.344 per usable Wh at the $599 ChatGPT showed, or $0.384 at FOSSiBOT's own store price of $669 today (over the $600 budget). On the light loads a 2 kWh buyer typically runs (fridge, CPAP, router), techtest.org's 100 W AC result means about 15 hours, not the 17.4 hours the 85% rule gives. A shopper who needs a true 2,000 Wh at the outlet needs roughly 2,350 Wh rated (2,000 ÷ 0.85), which no listing in this price band offers. No equivalent light-load measurement was found for the DYNESS, Jackery 2000 v2, Anker F2000 or Growatt, so the finding does not rank them against each other.

findings.label: Maker's runtime formula (usable AC energy factor)
findings.value: Working time = Watt-Hours × 0.85 ÷ device watts, so 1,741 Wh usable of 2,048 Wh
findings.note: Verbatim: "Working time = F2400's Watt-Hours * 0.85 / operating power of your device." The FAQ adds "The data is theretical lab data. Please note the actual power consumption varies based on many factors." Arithmetic: 2,048 × 0.85 = 1,740.8 Wh. The same sentence is on https://eu.fossibot.com/pages/general-questions-faq (read 2026-11-11).

findings.label: Measured usable capacity, 100 W load from the AC outlet
findings.source_title: FOSSiBOT F2400 Powerstation Test: Leistung, Kapazität und Effizienz im Überblick (techtest.org, Michael Barton, 2024-07-03)
findings.note: Lowest figure in the test: "bei einer Last von lediglich 100W über die Steckdose gemessen". German site, so the unit was probably the 230 V version; the article summary did not say. Arithmetic: 1,512 ÷ 100 W = 15.1 h, against 17.4 h from the maker's 0.85 formula. $599 ÷ 1,512 = $0.396 per delivered Wh at this load.

findings.label: Measured usable capacity, 100 W load from USB-C
findings.source_title: FOSSiBOT F2400 Powerstation Test (techtest.org, Michael Barton)
findings.note: Best figure in the test: "schwankte die nutzbare Kapazität der F2400 zwischen 1512 Wh und 1807 Wh". Barton reports efficiency between 76% and 98% depending on load. Derived, not measured: the AC path lost 295 Wh more than USB-C at the same 100 W; over 15.1 h that is about 19.5 W of extra loss with the inverter running.

findings.label: Measured AC recharge time against the maker's claim
findings.value: About 2 h 45 min at the 1,100 W setting and about 3 h 45 min at 700 W; the maker claims 0 to 100% in 2 hours
findings.source_title: FOSSiBOT F2400 Powerstation Test (techtest.org, Michael Barton)
findings.note: Barton also saw the charge rate dip after about 30 minutes at 1,100 W, possibly thermal, and not at 700 W. The 2-hour claim is from the store listing at https://www.fossibot.com/products/fossibot-f2400 (read 2026-11-11 through storecheck search). Arithmetic: 2,048 Wh ÷ 1,100 W = 1.86 h before losses and taper.

findings.label: AC charge-rate dial and solar input
findings.value: Front dial limits AC input from 300 W to 1,100 W in 200 W steps; solar input 500 W max, 11.5–50 V, 20 A; UPS switchover under 10 ms
findings.source_title: Leistungsstarke 2.400-W-Powerstation mit unterbrechungsfreier Stromversorgung: FossiBot F2400 im Test (Notebookcheck, Christian Hintze, 2025-05-27)
findings.note: These are rated values as reported by Notebookcheck; it measured no capacity. techtest.org lists the same five dial steps (300, 500, 700, 900, 1,100 W). The dial lets the unit recharge on a shared household circuit or a small generator.

findings.label: Price at the maker's US store
findings.note: From storecheck.py search on https://www.fossibot.com; the product call returned HTTP 429 twice. The listing also says "2048Wh Capacity | 2400W AC Pure Sine Wave Inverter (4800W Surge)", "4,000+ Life Cycles to 80%", "10ms uninterruptible home backup UPS" and "5-Year full-device warranty". ChatGPT's $599 is an Amazon-tracked price, which I did not check. Arithmetic: $669 ÷ 1,740.8 Wh = $0.384 per usable Wh; $599 ÷ 1,740.8 = $0.344.

findings.label: What the cited rival says about losses
findings.value: A 1,000 Wh station runs a 100 W fridge about 8.5 hours "after inverter losses"; sizing advice is "multiply by 1.3 for inverter losses and a reserve"
findings.source_title: Cheapest Portable Power Station per Wh — November 2026 Amazon Price Comparison
findings.note: Read through https://r.jina.ai/https://cheapestwh.com/ because the direct fetch failed on a certificate error. The page ranks on rated Wh: F2400 $599.00 ($0.292/Wh), Growatt INFINITY 2000 Pro $648.00, BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 $898.99, Jackery Explorer 2000 v2 $999.00. Those are the rival's tracked Amazon prices, not checked by me. Its generic rule gives 17.4 h for 2,048 Wh at 100 W; techtest.org's measurement gives 15.1 h for the F2400.

findings.label: Deal thread content
findings.value: $516 with free shipping through AliExpress, after a $100 clip coupon plus code BYE100F; 2,048 Wh LiFePO4, 2,400 W rated, 4,800 W peak
findings.source_title: ECO-WORTHY PS2400 2400W 2048Wh LiFePO4 Portable Power Station $516 + Free Shipping
findings.note: A coupon-stacked deal price, not the maker's store price. The thread gives no usable-capacity, efficiency or idle figure.

findings.label: Price at the maker's US store (solar bundle only)
findings.value: $1,199.00 for Elite 200 V2 + 200 W solar panel
findings.note: From storecheck.py search on https://www.bluettipower.com. The search returned bundles only, not the standalone station. The bundle is well over the $600 budget.
